summary: Preserved candidate PR 2856's valid selective dequantization and tests, independently reproduced the remaining MI gfx950 heuristic counterexamples, and rejected a synchronization-based overlap discriminator after it worsened latency. No further default-policy source change is justified without executing the target NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell FlashMLA path.

tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950, random 8/16/24/32-query compact cases measured 1.012x/1.126x/1.239x/1.285x warmed full latency. The default shared 33-query case used the 150994944-byte full buffer; forcing the 2048-row union peaked at 4930048 bytes.
Four exact-candidate GPU tests passed: independent FP8 numerical reference, physical alias deduplication/remapping, fallback behavior, pre-dedup gate, and invalid sentinels.
At 262144 logical rows and 8 queries, the candidate selected 4029 compact rows, reduced BF16 staging from 301989888 to 4641408 bytes, and measured a 2.540x speedup.

The flashmla_sparse and flashmla_kv subtests stopped before attention because the available HIP legacy DSA path requires page_size == 1 while the fixture uses 64; one compatible subtest passed and unsupported variants skipped.

gpu_evidence: Checked-out Python/Triton source compiled with private caches and ran on one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2.
remaining_limitations: BF16 flashmla_sparse attention output correctness and end-to-end sparse-prefill performance remain unverified because the assigned AMD gfx950 device is not NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell.
The ROCm integration fixture stops before attention because page size 64 is unsupported by the available legacy HIP DSA path, which requires page size 1.
The candidate's fixed gate still selects slower compact staging for some 131072-row inputs and rejects a complete-overlap 33-query union with a large memory benefit.

Determining overlap before deduplication requires additional device work and a host-visible policy decision in the current Python implementation; the tested torch.equal discriminator measurably worsened both fallback and shared-case latency.
No C++, CUDA, HIP, or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
